- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.3), model tends to over-forecast; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% relative to prior peak.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+2% from 14d avg), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +1.5% above recent high.
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (avg > -0.1), model under-reacts to true volatility; increase forecast by 0.5–1.0% to align with sentiment momentum.
- Mean reversion bias: if 30d forecast is >+1.5% above 18d history, reduce by 0.5–1.0% to avoid over-leveraging bullish sentiment.
- For 30d horizon, model often lags true price by 2–4 days; adjust forecast to be 0.5–1.0% higher than 18d history if sentiment is trending up.
- If sentiment is negative and forecast is rising, reduce forecast slope by 0.2–0.4% per day to avoid “sentiment reversal” overfitting.
